lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Replace or remove the code URL if it is a placeholder.
items.because: A broken link is worse than no link.

items.says: Specify whether the 35% accuracy improvement is relative or a percentage-point gain.
items.because: The distinction affects how impressive and believable the result is.

items.says: Identify the evaluation set or baseline for the accuracy improvement.
items.because: Those details determine how believable the result is.

items.says: Clarify what reviewer disagreement measures and whether 14% to 6% is a change in disagreement rate.
Explain the reviewer’s independence.
items.because: The routing layer restricts what the reviewer can see.

items.says: State the comparison conditions for “equal accuracy.”
items.because: That would make the tool-call and latency reductions easier to trust.

items.says: Use a consistent spelling convention for “penalises.”
items.because: It differs from the otherwise US-oriented presentation.

items.says: Clarify the release decision the evaluation harness supported.
items.because: Readers should understand how checkpoint testing prevented the regressions from shipping.

items.says: The adapter fine-tuning bullet repeats the first bullet.
The claim about learning to reproduce tool outputs appears at odds with assistant-only loss masking.
Clarify how the backlog reduction was attributed to the triage branch.
items.because: The reduction may have simply occurred in the eight weeks after launch.

items.says: The stated switch from FP32 to BF16 alone does not generally explain a 4× GPU-memory reduction.
items.because: Other changes may have been involved.

items.says: Specify the load-test conditions if they matter to the latency comparison.
Distinguish the measured latency improvement from the 200 ms CI threshold.
“Maintained” and “adds” have mismatched tenses.
Clarify whether the regression checks caused the three-day release cycle or were one contributing change.
Quantify the backlog or dispatch improvement if possible.
Link the repository from the header or project entry if it is public.
items.because: “Owner” is less informative than a link to the work.

items.says: Name concrete AI-first practices, your role, and a measured result, or remove the bullet.
items.because: It is much vaguer than the two technical bullets beneath it.

items.says: Define what the 100× comparison measures.
Explain what the stress test demonstrates in practice.
items.because: Otherwise, it may read as an impressive-sounding synthetic benchmark without a practical outcome.

items.says: Say how you verified that the deadlocks and lost results were resolved under 50-way fan-out, if space allows.
Link the contribution if it is public.
items.because: That would help substantiate the open-source role.

items.says: Identify what you contributed beyond wiring existing metrics into the module, if applicable.
Specify what the Kendall correlation compares.
items.because: The result is compelling once its meaning is clear.

items.says: Explain how the 400-plus trials were constructed.
items.because: The result is compelling once its meaning is clear.

items.says: The backlog accomplishment duplicates the Mobility Systems bullet.
The backlog accomplishment does not belong under the evaluation project.
Put Git with tooling rather than programming languages, or remove it if space is tight.
Group Kubernetes separately from ML methods.
Use one date style throughout.
